title: Overview
text: ChatRelay keeps your AI coding chats on all your devices and carries a project s context from one AI tool to the next. Your history goes to storage you own: a folder or a private GitHub repository. There is no ChatRelay server. # What you can do Sync between devices. Start on your desktop and pick up on your laptop, with every file path changed to the new machine. See Sync between devices . Search everything. Find any prompt or answer in every project and every tool, in under a second. See Search and usage . Continue in another tool. Summarize a project into a HANDOFF.md , or give the next tool the context it needs. See Summaries and handoff . Read anywhere. Open your chats in the web viewer or the Android app. See Web and phone viewer . Stay safe. Backups before every write, a dry run before every download, and optional end-to-end encryption. See Security . # Works with your AI tools Tool Versions On your other devices Claude Code Terminal, VS Code Restored into Claude Code Codex Terminal, VS Code, desktop app Restored into Codex Cursor Editor, CLI Open in ChatRelay Kiro Editor, CLI Open in ChatRelay Antigravity IDE, CLI Open in ChatRelay Every chat can be viewed, searched, summarized and synced. See Supported AI tools for the details. # Where to go next Install ChatRelay on your first device. Follow the first-time setup and choose your storage . Set up your second device . Something not working? Start with Troubleshooting .

title: Install
text: # Windows Download ChatRelay_ version _x64-setup.exe from the latest release . Run it. The installer is not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may say Windows protected your PC : click More info → Run anyway . You only install once. Later versions arrive by themselves (see Updates ). The app installs per user in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatRelay\ . It starts in the system tray. Closing the window keeps it running there; use Quit in the tray menu to stop it. # Android (viewer) Download ChatRelay_ version .apk from the same release page and open it on your phone (allow install unknown apps for your browser or file manager when asked). The Android app is a read-only viewer of your GitHub storage; a phone has no AI tool history of its own. # macOS and Linux A GitHub Actions workflow ( .github/workflows/desktop-mac-linux.yml ) builds a macOS (Apple silicon) .dmg and a Linux .AppImage and .deb , and can add them, with their update entries, to a release. They are not code-signed (macOS: right-click → Open the first time) and have had little testing. # Web The web viewer is a static page you can host yourself (GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify…) or run locally. See Web and phone viewer .

title: First-time setup
text: When ChatRelay opens for the first time, a setup wizard walks you through these steps. You can run it again any time from the command palette ( Ctrl+Shift+P → Run First-time Setup Again ). Your history. ChatRelay finds Claude Code s history in %USERPROFILE%\.claude\projects (or the folder in CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ) and Codex s in %USERPROFILE%\.codex (or CODEX_HOME ). It also finds your Cursor, Kiro and Antigravity chats, and shows how many conversations it found per tool. Claude Code s 30-day deletion. By default Claude Code deletes conversations older than 30 days ( cleanupPeriodDays ). ChatRelay shows this and offers to raise it. It backs up settings.json before changing it. Machine name. For example DESKTOP or LAPTOP . It is shown next to every conversation, so you know which PC it came from. Storage (backend). A folder (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, network drive) or a private GitHub repository. See the next section. Anthropic API key (optional). Only needed for summaries. It is stored in the Windows Credential Manager (OS keychain), never in a file. Auto-sync. Turns on automatic upload/download (Claude Code hooks plus the background timer). Upload everything. Optionally uploads your whole existing history right away, with a progress bar.

title: Choose your storage

heads.text: Option B: a private GitHub repository

text: Your history goes to a place you control. ChatRelay has no server of its own. # Option A: a folder Any folder that your other PCs can also see: Google Drive for desktop, e.g. G:\My Drive\chatrelay OneDrive, e.g. %OneDrive%\chatrelay Dropbox, a NAS or network share, or a USB drive you carry Only compressed copies go there. Your live ~/.claude and ~/.codex folders are never moved into a cloud folder. The folder backend also keeps the previous versions of each file ( Settings → What to sync → Versions kept (folder backend) , default 2). # Option B: a private GitHub repository Best if you also want the web or phone viewer. Sign in with GitHub (recommended). ChatRelay shows a short code; you enter it on github.com and approve. The ChatRelay GitHub App only gets access to the repositories you choose (normally just your history repository), with permission to read and write their contents. No password is stored, and no server is involved. Or paste a personal access token (classic token with repo scope, or a fine-grained token with Contents: Read and write on that one repo). If you are logged in with the GitHub CLI ( gh auth login ), ChatRelay can use that token. Pick an existing private repository or click Create private repo . Public repositories are refused, because chat history can contain private code and secrets. On GitHub, each upload is one commit . Files bigger than 40 MB (compressed) are split into parts automatically, because GitHub refuses single files over 100 MB. The token lives only in the OS keychain (service chatrelay ).

title: Set up your second device
text: On PC 1 (the one that already has the history): Install ChatRelay and choose a backend. Upload: click Upload now in the Simple view (or Upload everything at the end of setup), or Push on a project in the Advanced view. A preview shows each conversation and any secrets found; you can choose to hide (redact) them in the uploaded copy. On PC 2 : Install ChatRelay and choose the same backend (the same synced folder, or the same GitHub repo). Put the project folder on PC 2 (for example with git clone ). The path may differ, for example D:\work\shop instead of C:\Users\me\shop . Click Bring history to this PC (Simple view), or open the Sync view (Advanced view). ChatRelay lists every project in the backend and where it would go on this PC: Git projects are matched automatically by their remote URL. Other projects : click Import into… / Link and pick the local folder once. The link is remembered. Check the dry run : which files will be written and every path change (for example ×166 C:\Users\me\shop → D:\work\shop ). Then confirm. Open the conversation in the tool: claude --resume or the VS Code Claude panel; codex resume or the Codex sidebar. For Codex: close Codex first (CLI, VS Code extension and desktop app). ChatRelay never writes to Codex s files while it is running; that conversation is skipped with the reason Codex is running , and comes in the next time. Turn on Auto-sync on both PCs and you don t need to do any of this by hand again.

title: Sync between devices

heads.text: Keep a project on this PC only

text: # Push and pull Push uploads the conversations of a project that changed since the last sync. Push all does every project. Pull downloads what s new. It always starts with a dry run that lists every file it would write and every path rewrite. Nothing is written until you confirm. # Auto-sync When Auto-sync is on: Claude Code : hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json run ChatRelay when a Claude Code session starts (pull) and ends (push). Codex : Codex has no such hook. The desktop app watches Codex s sessions and uploads a changed conversation about a minute after it goes quiet. Every 15 minutes (starting 20 seconds after launch) it also downloads new ones (skipped while Codex is running). Uploads that failed because you were offline are queued and retried. You can turn auto-sync on or off in Settings, in the tray menu, or with chatrelay hooks install|uninstall . # Status dots Dot Meaning What to do Green Synced Nothing Yellow / orange Changes on this PC not uploaded yet Push, or wait for auto-sync Red Last sync failed Open Logs for the reason Grey Never synced Push it once Hollow circle No project identity yet (not linked) Push it (a link is created) or Link it to the project from the other PC Crossed-out circle Sync is off for this project on this PC Turn sync on on the project s page, if you want it synced again # Keep a project on this PC only Some projects should never leave a PC, for example client work that must stay on one machine. On the project s page click Don t sync (or hover a project in the Simple view and click don t sync ). From then on nothing from that project is uploaded, and it is not downloaded automatically (auto-sync hooks, background sync, Upload everything ). A manual Pull still works. The project shows a crossed-out status dot and sync off on this PC ; Turn sync on undoes it. From the command line: chatrelay exclude dir ( --remove to undo, no folder to list them). # Backups Every write is preceded by a backup in ~/.chatrelay/backups/ timestamp - what / . Open Backups (or chatrelay backups ) to see them, and Restore one to put every file back exactly as it was. A restore also removes files that the change had created. # Logs Logs shows everything ChatRelay did, with errors highlighted, and a button that copies an error report. # Tray menu Push now · Pull now · Auto-sync on/off · Last sync status · Open · Quit.

title: The app
text: # Simple view and Advanced view Simple view (default), in sections: the status of your history; Sync ( Upload now , Bring history to this PC , the auto-sync switch); Projects on this PC , with filters (to upload, not uploaded, backed up, sync off), a search box and when each was last used; and Help . Advanced view : a VS Code-like layout with an activity bar (Projects Ctrl+Shift+E , Sync Ctrl+Shift+Y , Summaries, Logs, Backups, Settings), tabs, a status bar and a command palette ( Ctrl+Shift+P ) with every action. Switch between them with Ctrl+Shift+P → Switch to Simple/Advanced View . # Conversations from several tools Every conversation has a small badge with its tool ( Claude , Codex , Cursor , Kiro or Antigravity ). Projects where you used more than one tool show a filter (All, or one tool). Opening a conversation shows the full transcript: your messages, the assistant s answers, tool calls (commands run, files edited) and the list of changed files.

title: Summaries and handoff

heads.text: Continue a conversation in the other tool

text: 🔒 Secrets never reach the AI. Before anything is sent to the model, ChatRelay replaces keys, tokens and passwords found in the chats (API keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, GitHub, AWS, Google, Slack, Stripe, Hugging Face, npm, SendGrid, Telegram bots; JWTs; private keys; PASSWORD=… -style lines; passwords inside URLs) with [REDACTED:kind] . This always happens and can t be turned off; the screen shows how many were hidden. Your code and the rest of the conversation are still sent, so for private or client code prefer a paid model whose provider doesn t keep data. Open Summaries (Advanced view), pick a project, tick the conversations (from any tool) and a model, then click Generate handoff . Models: Your logins, no API key: Claude Code · Sonnet / Opus and Codex run through the Claude Code or Codex already installed and signed in on this PC, with your own plan. They appear only when that tool is installed. The summary runs in an empty temporary folder with no tools, and nothing is saved to that tool s history. Claude API (Anthropic API key in Settings → Secrets ): Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.1. OpenRouter (OpenRouter API key): an automatic free model, Nemotron 3 Ultra, Gemma 4 31B and MiniMax M3.1 Flash (free), DeepSeek V4 Flash (paid, very cheap). Any OpenRouter model works from the CLI with --model openrouter: id . Before anything is sent, ChatRelay shows what will be sent and to whom, which secrets it found and hid, and asks you to confirm. On top of the secret patterns, the values in the project s .env files and everything in your Settings → Never send list (client names, internal hosts, …) are hidden by exact match. The history is condensed first: your requests, the assistant s final answer of each turn, and the files changed. Long tool output and thinking are dropped. Conversations from all tools are merged in time order and labelled with their tool. Long histories are summarized in ~100k-token parts and then merged. The result has these sections: Project overview, What s done, Key decisions, Open bugs / known issues, Next steps, Files touched. Then you can: Save HANDOFF.md in the project folder, or Continue in… a tool: choose Claude Code ( CLAUDE.md ), Codex ( AGENTS.md ) or Gemini CLI ( GEMINI.md ). The list shows the tools installed on this PC. ChatRelay adds a short Previous context section (overview, what s done, next steps) to that file. Running it again replaces only its own section; the rest of the file is untouched. Or copy the text. From the command line: chatrelay summarize --target handoff|claude-md|agents-md|gemini-md|none . # Continue a conversation in the other tool Open a conversation and click Continue in Claude Code (on a Codex conversation) or Continue in Codex (on a Claude Code one). ChatRelay adds a new conversation to that tool in the same project, with every prompt and answer; tool calls and changed files appear as short notes, because the two tools record them differently. Then open the project and run claude --resume or codex resume (or pick it in the VS Code panel). The original conversation is not changed, and nothing is written while the target tool is running. # Share a conversation Open a conversation and click Share : copy it as Markdown, save a .md file, Save as PDF (the print dialog s Save as PDF ), or Create link , a secret GitHub Gist that anyone with the link can read. Prompts and answers are included (tool calls if you tick it; thinking and tool output never), and keys, passwords, the project s .env values and your never send list are hidden first. A link needs a GitHub token with the gist scope: the GitHub CLI s login is used if you have one, or add one in Settings → Secrets → GitHub gist token .

title: Search and usage
text: # Search every conversation Open Search in the activity bar ( Ctrl+Shift+F ) and type a few words. ChatRelay finds every prompt you wrote and every answer the assistant gave that contains all of them, in every project and every tool, newest first and grouped by conversation, with the words highlighted. Click a match to open that conversation with the words already in its find box. Tool output (file contents, command output) is not searched. The first search reads your history once (under a second for about 2 GB); after that results are instant. From the command line: chatrelay search words . # Usage Usage in the activity bar shows, for the last 7, 30 or 90 days: Conversations, messages, tokens and active days, each compared with the period before, plus your current and longest streak. Activity per day, as conversations, messages or tokens, split by tool. When you work: a weekday × hour map. Tokens: how many the AI wrote, new input, and how many were read from or written to the cache, by model. Your projects and longest conversations; click one to open it. Copy report copies it all as Markdown. Token counts come from Claude Code and Codex; Antigravity, Cursor and Kiro don t record them. It is worked out on this PC; nothing is sent.

title: Web and phone viewer
text: 🌐 Live web viewer: https://abh1shxkk.github.io/chatrelay-web/ A read-only version of the app that opens the history in your GitHub backend from any browser or from the Android app: projects, conversations from every tool, and full transcripts. It uses the same Rust engine compiled to WebAssembly, so it shows exactly what the desktop app shows. Uploading, downloading, auto-sync and summaries stay in the desktop app, because they need the local history folders. Sign in with GitHub, or with your repo name and a fine-grained token limited to that repo with Contents: Read-only . The token is kept only in that browser (localStorage if you tick remember , otherwise sessionStorage). The page only talks to api.github.com and loads no third-party scripts. The first visit reads each conversation once to count messages; results are cached by content hash. On phone-sized screens the layout switches to a single pane: list → project → transcript, with a back button and a bottom bar.

title: Updates
text: The desktop app checks for a new version when it starts, every time its window is opened, every hour, when you come back to its window after 5 minutes or more, and when you click Check for updates (Settings → About, the Simple view, or the command palette). It shows a spinner while checking. When one is available you see A new version is available → Update now . The app downloads it, verifies its signature (apps only accept updates signed with the project s key), installs it in place and restarts. History and settings are kept. The Android app shows a notice with a link to the new APK.

title: Supported AI tools
text: All tools 5 Restores into the tool 2 Opens in ChatRelay 3 Claude Code Restores into the tool Terminal CLI VS Code extension Sync Automatic, when a session starts and ends Open your chats claude --resume or VS Code history Context file CLAUDE.md OpenAI Codex Restores into the tool Codex CLI VS Code extension Desktop app Sync Uploads a minute after a chat goes quiet, downloads every 15 minutes Open your chats codex resume or the Codex sidebar Context file AGENTS.md Cursor Opens in ChatRelay Editor (Agent chat) Cursor CLI Sync Your chats reach every device Open your chats ChatRelay on desktop, web and phone Context file AGENTS.md Kiro Opens in ChatRelay Editor (agent chat) Kiro CLI Sync Your chats reach every device Open your chats ChatRelay on desktop, web and phone Context file AGENTS.md Antigravity Opens in ChatRelay Antigravity IDE Antigravity CLI Sync Your chats reach every device Open your chats ChatRelay on desktop, web and phone Context file GEMINI.md # Compare Feature Claude Code Codex Cursor Kiro Antigravity View chats Search Summarize Sync between devices Web and phone viewer CLI chats Restore into the tool – – – Auto-sync Token counts – – – Each tool keeps its history in its own undocumented format, and those formats change between versions. So ChatRelay checks the format it finds on your PC. If it sees a version it doesn t know, it still shows the conversations, but turns off writing for that tool and tells you why in Settings → AI tools . It never guesses. Verified versions: Claude Code 2.1.x; Codex 0.144 to 0.160 (index database state_5.sqlite , schema migration 58); Antigravity 2.6; Cursor 3.28 and its CLI; Kiro 1.4 and Kiro CLI 3.1. # Codex support in detail What travels with each Codex conversation: Item Where Codex keeps it What ChatRelay does The conversation ( rollout ) ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout- time - id .jsonl (some versions write .jsonl.zst , compressed) Copied, every path rewritten The thread s index row ~/.codex/state_5.sqlite , table threads Added or updated so the conversation appears in codex resume and the sidebar The thread s name ~/.codex/session_index.jsonl Added Codex memory for that thread ~/.codex/memories_1.sqlite , table stage1_outputs Added if this PC has none for that thread; paths rewritten Goals of that thread ~/.codex/goals_1.sqlite , tables thread_goals , thread_goal_continuation_deferrals Added if this PC has none for that thread Details that matter: Codex must be closed while ChatRelay writes. ChatRelay checks for running codex processes (CLI, VS Code extension, desktop app). It does not ask you to close anything during background sync; it just tries again later. History mode is kept. Newer Codex versions store paginated history; Codex rebuilds its page database ( thread_history_*.sqlite ) from the conversation file the first time you open it, so ChatRelay never writes that database. Your own settings for a thread stay yours. On update, this PC s pinned state, custom name, archive state and account are kept. Folders and sections that only exist on the other PC are cleared. Account. An imported thread is assigned to the Codex account that owns most threads on this PC. Windows path prefix. Codex on Windows stores working folders as \\?\D:\project . ChatRelay adds that prefix only to Windows paths on a PC whose Codex uses it, and never to macOS or Linux paths. Compressed conversations ( .jsonl.zst ) can be read and updated. On update the file is replaced by a plain .jsonl (the compressed original is backed up first). Memory bookkeeping that belongs to the other PC (how often a memory was used, whether it was picked for consolidation) is not copied. Unknown versions. If Codex s index uses a database ChatRelay doesn t know (for example a future state_6.sqlite ), or adds a required field it can t fill, writing is turned off for Codex with a clear warning. Reading still works.

title: CLI reference
text: The installer puts chatrelay.exe next to the app ( %LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatRelay\ ). It is what the Claude Code hooks run. Add that folder to your PATH to use it anywhere. From source: cargo run -p chatrelay-cli -- … . text Copy chatrelay scan [--json] List projects sessions chatrelay status [--json] Backend, last sync, hooks, queue, cleanupPeriodDays chatrelay push [--cwd dir ] [--all] [--dry-run] [--redact] chatrelay pull [--cwd dir ] [--project id ] [--all] [--dry-run] chatrelay summarize [--cwd dir ] [--model id ] [--target handoff|claude-md|agents-md|gemini-md|none] chatrelay remote List projects stored in the backend chatrelay link dir projectId Link a local folder to a remote project ID (--remove to unlink) chatrelay search words… [--json] Search every conversation (prompts and answers) on this PC chatrelay storage [--compact] Space used by the GitHub store; --compact removes old versions chatrelay usage [--days N] [--json] Tokens used by Claude Code and Codex on this PC, by model chatrelay exclude [ dir ] [--remove] Turn sync off (or back on) for a project on this PC; no dir lists them chatrelay config [key] [value] Show or set config (machineName, backend.folder, backend.github, secretScan, ...) chatrelay secret set github-token|anthropic-api-key value chatrelay hooks install|uninstall Add/remove the SessionStart/SessionEnd hooks chatrelay cleanup-days n Set Claude Code's cleanupPeriodDays (backs up settings.json) chatrelay backups [restore id ] List or restore backups chatrelay queue Retry queued (offline) pushes Any AI tool (provider = claude-code | codex | antigravity | cursor | kiro): chatrelay providers [--json] Which tools are installed, their version/format, import on/off chatrelay providers sessions provider [--cwd dir ] [--json] chatrelay providers show provider id [--json] Read a session in the tool-neutral format chatrelay providers export provider id --out file.json.gz chatrelay providers import file.json.gz --to dir [--dry-run] Flags: --hook (read Claude Code hook JSON from stdin; never fails), --quiet, --json, --verbose Exit codes: 0 OK, 1 error, 2 push had conflicts (pull first). Environment variables: Variable Effect CHATRELAY_HOME ChatRelay s own data folder (default ~/.chatrelay ) CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR Claude Code s folder (default ~/.claude ) CODEX_HOME Codex s folder (default ~/.codex ) ANTHROPIC_API_KEY Used for summaries when no key is saved in the keychain GITHUB_TOKEN Used by the release script

text: Where What ~/.chatrelay/config.json Machine name and ID, backend, links, options ~/.chatrelay/state.json Per-session sync bookkeeping (hashes and sizes last pushed/pulled) ~/.chatrelay/backups/ Timestamped backups ~/.chatrelay/logs/chatrelay.log JSON-lines log (Logs panel, copyable error report) ~/.chatrelay/queue.json Pushes waiting for the backend ~/.chatrelay/scan-cache.json Scan cache (sizes, times, titles) OS keychain, service chatrelay github-token , anthropic-api-key ~/.claude/projects/… Claude Code conversations (read; written on pull) ~/.claude/settings.json Only for auto-sync hooks and cleanupPeriodDays (backed up first) ~/.codex/sessions/… , state_5.sqlite , session_index.jsonl , memories_1.sqlite , goals_1.sqlite Codex conversations and their index (read; written on pull, only while Codex is closed, backed up first) project /.chatrelay.json Only for non-git projects pushed from a project screen project /HANDOFF.md , CLAUDE.md , AGENTS.md , GEMINI.md Only when you save a summary there

title: How it works

heads.text: Storage layout (in the folder or repo)

text: # Where Claude Code keeps history Path What ~/.claude/projects/ encoded-path / session-uuid .jsonl One file per session, one JSON object per line ~/.claude/projects/ encoded-path / session-uuid /subagents/*.jsonl + *.meta.json Subagent transcripts (synced as a sidecar ) ~/.claude/projects/ encoded-path / session-uuid /tool-results/* Large tool outputs saved to disk (sidecar) ~/.claude/projects/ encoded-path /memory/ Project auto-memory ( MEMORY.md + notes) Things that differ from the usual assumptions, all handled: Drive-letter case differs by client. The VS Code extension records c:\Users\… (folder c--Users-… ), the CLI records C:\Users\… (folder C--Users-… ), and one session can contain both. On Windows, paths are compared case-insensitively. Folder names can t be decoded reliably. C:\Users\me\my project and C:\Users\me\my-project both encode to C--Users-me-my-project . The real path comes from the cwd recorded in the sessions; decoding the name is only a labelled fallback. Sessions can be huge (200+ MB with embedded images/PDFs), so everything is streamed. Scan results are cached by size and modification time, so a rescan takes about 100 ms. One assistant reply spans several lines (one per content block, same message.id ); message counts de-duplicate them. Titles come from the first real prompt (IDE wrapper tags stripped); Claude Code s own ai-title is shown next to it. Many line types besides user/assistant ( attachment , file-history-snapshot , queue-operation , ai-title , last-prompt , permission-mode , …). Unknown types and fields are kept untouched. # Where Codex keeps history See Codex support in detail . Each line of a rollout is {timestamp, type, payload} ; the first is session_meta with the session id and cwd . Codex has written conversations in three generations ( event_msg/item_completed items in ≥0.15x, user_message / agent_message events earlier, plain response_item messages in the oldest); the viewer uses the richest one present. # Adapters Each AI tool is an adapter ( crates/core/src/providers/ ) behind one interface ( ProviderAdapter ): detect the tool and its format, list projects and sessions, read a session into a tool-neutral shape ( UniversalSession ), export it losslessly ( SessionBundle : the original files plus tool metadata such as the Codex index row), import it on another PC (rewrite paths, check the tool isn t running, back up, dry run), and append new lines. See Adding another AI tool . # Project identity The same project has a different path on each PC, so it is identified by, in order: A manual link (Link button / chatrelay link dir id ), stored in ChatRelay s config The git remote , normalized: git@github.com:Me/Repo.git and https://github.com/me/repo both become git:github.com/me/repo A .chatrelay.json in the project root holding a UUID, created on first push for non-git projects (commit it, or link manually on the other PC). Upload everything and background sync create a link in ChatRelay s config instead, so nothing is written into your project folders. # Storage layout (in the folder or repo) text Copy projectId-slug / manifest.json machines, original paths, hashes, timestamps, revision sessionId .jsonl.gz Claude Code session (whole, or its start when deltas exist) sessionId .d N .jsonl.gz lines appended after that, one blob per push sessionId .sidecar.json.gz subagents/ + tool-results/ (if any) memory.json.gz Claude Code project memory (if any) provider - sessionId .bundle.json.gz another tool's session (e.g. codex-…): files + metadata provider - sessionId .d N .jsonl.gz lines appended to it later .versions/ file / timestamp previous versions (folder backend) Other tools sessions are listed under providerSessions in the manifest (key provider : id ). Older versions of the app ignore that list and keep it intact. # Push Sessions are compared by SHA-256; only new or changed ones are uploaded. Originals are only ever read. Only new lines are sent. AI tools only ever append to a conversation file, so after a session s first upload a push stores just the lines added since the last sync as a delta part. Each part records the paths of the machine that pushed it. Session hashes are chained ( hash = sha256(previous : sha256(part)) ). After 40 parts the next push uploads the whole session again. When the shortcut doesn t apply (the file changed some other way, a conflict, state from an older version) the whole file is uploaded. If the backend has a version you haven t seen that contains messages you don t have, that session s push is refused with pull first , so nothing is lost. Offline? (GitHub unreachable, the cloud drive not mounted.) The push is queued in ~/.chatrelay/queue.json and retried on the next run and every 15 minutes by the desktop app. # Pull Paths are rewritten inside parsed JSON (string values and object keys), so JSON escaping is never a problem. Forms handled: Windows paths as C:\… , c:/… , Git-Bash /c/… and WSL /mnt/c/… (case-insensitive); POSIX paths (case-sensitive); file:/// URLs including %20 -encoded spaces; separators after the project root are converted when moving between operating systems; the tool s own home folder ( ~/.claude , ~/.codex ) and Claude Code s encoded folder name are rewritten too. Sibling folders such as shop-old are never touched. Fast path: a PC that has exactly what it last synced downloads only the missing parts and appends them. Divergence (conversations are append-only, compared by line ids for Claude Code and by text prefix for other tools): remote contains local → update local contains remote → yours is newer and is kept (uploaded on the next push) both changed → conflict : your copy stays as it is, and the other version is saved as a new conversation with a new id (Codex: named (from ) ). Both then appear in the tool and sync to your other PCs. # Auto-sync hooks (Claude Code) Enable auto-sync merges this into ~/.claude/settings.json ; your other settings and hooks are kept, and a backup is made first: json Copy hooks : { SessionStart : [ { hooks : [ { type : command , command : \ …/ChatRelay/chatrelay.exe\ pull --hook --quiet --chatrelay-hook , timeout : 60 } ] } ] , SessionEnd : [ { hooks : [ { type : command , command : \ …/ChatRelay/chatrelay.exe\ push --hook --quiet --chatrelay-hook , timeout : 60 } ] } ] } --hook reads Claude Code s hook JSON from stdin ( cwd , session_id ), falling back to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR and then the working directory. Hooks always exit 0 , so they can never break a session; errors go to the Logs panel. The hook runs the native chatrelay executable installed next to the app. No Node.js needed. Disable auto-sync removes only the hooks containing the chatrelay-hook marker.

title: Security
text: Originals are never modified on upload. Uploading only reads your history files. Nothing is written while the tool is running (Codex). Claude Code s open session (the one that triggered the hook) is never touched. Backup before every write , including Claude Code s settings.json , Codex s databases (with their -wal and -shm files) and session_index.jsonl . Dry run for every import. You see every file and every path rewrite before anything happens. Both versions are kept on conflict , never overwritten. Secret scan. Before uploading, ChatRelay looks for API keys and passwords: Anthropic, OpenAI, GitHub, AWS, Google, Slack and Stripe keys, JWTs, private keys, .env -style SECRET=… lines, and credentials inside URLs. You choose: warn , redact (replaced with [REDACTED:kind] in the uploaded copy only), or off . Optional end-to-end encryption (GitHub storage). In Settings → Encryption set a password: from then on every file is encrypted on your PC (Argon2id key, XChaCha20-Poly1305) before it is uploaded, so GitHub and anyone who gets into the repository see only scrambled data. Enter the same password on each PC, and in the web viewer s or phone s Settings. A PC without it can t read or upload anything. If you forget the password, nobody can read the history , not even ChatRelay. Encrypt files stored before re-uploads older files encrypted; then Storage → Remove old versions deletes the unencrypted copies from the repository s history. Secrets stay in the OS keychain. Your GitHub token and Anthropic key are never written to a file. Your logins are never touched. ChatRelay does not read, copy or change Claude Code s or Codex s login files ( ~/.claude/.credentials.json , ~/.codex/auth.json , …). Syncing history cannot log you out. If you get logged out, it comes from the tool itself (for example an expired session or signing in with another account on another PC). Private storage only. Public GitHub repositories are refused. No ChatRelay server. Data only goes between your PCs, your folder or GitHub, and (only when you make a summary) the Anthropic API. Not synced, by design: ~/.claude/history.jsonl (your up-arrow prompt history across all projects), ~/.claude/file-history/ (rewind snapshots), and all credentials.

title: Privacy
text: ChatRelay is an app that runs on your own devices. It has no server and no account, and it does not collect anything about you. This page says exactly where your data goes. # What stays on your PC Your original chat history. ChatRelay only reads it when uploading. Your settings, sync state, backups and logs, in the ~/.chatrelay folder. Your GitHub token and API keys, in the keychain of your operating system. They are never written to a file. Your usage report. It is worked out on your PC and nothing is sent. ChatRelay never reads, copies or changes the login files of your AI tools. # What leaves your PC Data only moves when one of these happens: When What goes Where to You sync Compressed copies of your chats The folder or private GitHub repository you chose You make a summary The condensed chat text, with secrets hidden first The AI model you picked, after you confirm You share a conversation with a link That conversation, with secrets hidden first A secret GitHub Gist The app checks for updates A normal web request GitHub # Your choices Secret scan. Hide keys and passwords in what you upload: see Security . Encryption. With a password, GitHub only ever stores scrambled data. Don t sync. Keep a project on one PC only: see Keep a project on this PC only . Never send. Words and values that are hidden from summaries and shared conversations. # The web viewer The web viewer keeps your token only in that browser, talks only to api.github.com and loads no third-party scripts. # This website The landing page and these docs load their fonts from Google Fonts. They use no analytics and no cookies. The docs remember your light or dark theme in your browser. # Questions Email abhichauhan200504@gmail.com .

title: Troubleshooting
text: SmartScreen blocks the installer. The installer isn t code-signed. Click More info → Run anyway . A project shows a yellow dot. It has conversations on this PC that aren t uploaded yet. Push it, or turn on auto-sync. A project from my other PC doesn t appear / appears under a different name. Projects are matched by git remote, a .chatrelay.json , or a link. If the folders have different names and no git remote, use Link (or Import into… ) once and pick the right local folder. A Codex conversation was skipped: Codex is running . Close the Codex CLI, the VS Code extension s Codex panel (or VS Code) and the Codex desktop app, then pull again. Background sync retries by itself. Codex import is off: Unknown Codex index database / new required fields . Your Codex is newer than this ChatRelay version knows. Update ChatRelay. Your conversations are still visible. I see a conversation twice, one ending with (from DESKTOP) . It was continued on both PCs before they synced. Both versions are kept; delete the one you don t need in the tool. My old Claude Code conversations disappeared. Claude Code deletes conversations older than cleanupPeriodDays (default 30). Raise it in Settings (or chatrelay cleanup-days 3650 ). Already-uploaded conversations can be pulled back from the backend. Did syncing log me out of Claude? No. ChatRelay never reads or writes login files. See Safety and privacy . Upload is slow the first time. The first upload sends everything (compressed). After that only new lines are sent. Pull first when pushing. Another PC uploaded a newer version that yours doesn t contain. Pull, then push. Offline. Pushes are queued and retried automatically; chatrelay queue retries now. Something went wrong after a pull. Open Backups and restore the backup made just before it. Where do I find errors? The Logs view (copy an error report from there), or ~/.chatrelay/logs/chatrelay.log .

title: Known limitations
text: The Windows installer is not code-signed (SmartScreen warning). Only Windows is tested. macOS and Linux build but have no published installers. A conversation open on two PCs at the same time can t be merged live; it becomes a conflict copy. Codex has no session ended hook, so a Codex conversation is uploaded about a minute after it goes quiet, not the moment it ends. For paths longer than 200 characters Claude Code s exact folder-name hash isn t documented; ChatRelay prefers an existing folder whose sessions record the same cwd , and otherwise uses its own - hash suffix. The web and phone viewers are read-only and need the GitHub backend. # Roadmap Restoring Antigravity, Cursor and Kiro conversations into those tools. Code-signed installers; tested macOS and Linux builds.

title: About the rename
text: ChatRelay was called Claude Sync until v0.5.0. Since then every name has changed too: the app and its install folder ( %LOCALAPPDATA%\ChatRelay ), the chatrelay command, the ~/.chatrelay data folder, the CHATRELAY_* environment variables, .chatrelay.json project files, the keychain service chatrelay and the releases repository chatrelay-releases . Moving over from Claude Sync, once per PC: Quit Claude Sync (tray → Quit ) and uninstall it in Windows Settings → Apps . Rename the folder ~/.claude-sync to ~/.chatrelay . Your settings, sync state and backups come with it. Install ChatRelay, then turn Auto-sync on. This replaces the old Claude Sync hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json . Add your GitHub token and API keys again ( Settings → Secrets , or sign in with GitHub). They were saved in the keychain under the old name. Rename any .claude-sync.json in your project folders to .chatrelay.json . On Android, uninstall the old app before installing the new APK. Your history in GitHub or the sync folder does not change; nothing needs to be uploaded again.

title: Build from source
text: Requirements: Node.js 20+, Rust (stable), and on Windows the MSVC toolchain (Visual Studio Desktop development with C++ ). bash Copy git clone https://github.com/Abh1shxkk/chatrelay.git cd chatrelay npm install npm run tauri:dev # run the desktop app with hot reload npm run test :rust # cargo test --workspace: engine, adapters, push/pull, GitHub backend npm test # UI helper tests (vitest) npm run typecheck # TypeScript npm run tauri:build # installer in target/release/bundle/nsis/ Project layout: text Copy crates/core/ Rust engine: scanner, JSONL, path rewriting, sync, backends, hooks, summaries crates/core/src/providers/ AI tool adapters: claude_code.rs, codex.rs (+ codex_format.rs, browser-safe parsing) crates/core/src/provider_sync.rs other tools' sessions in push/pull (bundles, deltas, conflict copies) crates/core/tests/ integration tests with fixture files (tests/fixtures/codex, tests/fixtures/claude-code) crates/cli/ the `chatrelay` CLI (also what the Claude Code hooks run) crates/wasm/ the engine compiled to WebAssembly for the web and phone viewers src-tauri/ desktop app: window, tray, background sync, the API behind window.chatRelay src/renderer/ React + TypeScript + Tailwind UI (shared by desktop, web and phone) src/shared/ TypeScript types and helpers mobile/ Android / iOS shell around the web version (Tauri) scripts/ release, CLI staging, WASM build tests/ vitest tests; tests/web/mock-github.mjs for testing the web version Running a development copy next to an installed one: set a separate identifier and data folder, so it never touches your real settings: powershell Copy $env:TAURI_CONFIG = { identifier : com.chatrelay.dev , productName : ChatRelay Dev } $env:CHATRELAY_HOME = D:\tmp\chatrelay-dev npm run tauri:dev # Web version bash Copy rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version 0.2.129 # must match wasm-bindgen in Cargo.lock npm run web:wasm # rebuild the WebAssembly engine npm run web:dev # http://localhost:5175/web.html npm run web:build # static site in out/web/ (host on GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Netlify…) node tests/web/mock-github.mjs folder-backend serves a folder backend as a fake GitHub API (dev builds only: set localStorage[ chatrelay-web:apiBase ] = http://localhost:5176 and use the token test-token-123456 ). # Mobile app (Android, iOS) Android needs JDK 17, the Android SDK (platform 36, build-tools 36, NDK r27) and the Rust Android targets ( tauri android init installs those): powershell Copy $env:JAVA_HOME = jdk-17 ; $env:ANDROID_HOME = android-sdk ; $env:NDK_HOME = $env:ANDROID_HOME \ndk\ version npm run mobile:android:init # once: generates mobile/gen/android npm run mobile:android:apk # debug APK for a phone (arm64) adb install -r that apk npm run mobile:android:release # release APK/AAB, signed when CHATRELAY_KEYSTORE_PROPERTIES is set Release signing reads a properties file kept outside the repo , named by CHATRELAY_KEYSTORE_PROPERTIES : properties Copy storeFile = D:/dev/android-keys/chatrelay-release.jks storePassword = … keyAlias = chatrelay keyPassword = … Create the key once with keytool -genkeypair -keystore chatrelay-release.jks -alias chatrelay -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -validity 10000 and back it up: updates to an installed app must be signed with the same key. iOS needs a Mac with Xcode and rustup target add aarch64-apple-ios aarch64-apple-ios-sim : bash Copy npm install npm run web:wasm npm run mobile:ios:init npm run mobile:ios:dev npm run mobile:ios:build

title: Adapter guide
text: Verify the storage format on a real machine first : where sessions live, the line/record format, any index database and its schema, how the tool lists sessions, how it stores paths, which processes mean running . Write it down at the top of the adapter file. Add a ProviderId in crates/core/src/providers/mod.rs and a file providers/ tool .rs implementing ProviderAdapter : detect , list_projects , list_sessions , read_session , export_session , import_session , optionally append_session , context_file_name , process_names . Rules every adapter follows: refuse to write while the tool runs ( ensure_not_running ), back up every file before writing ( ImportOptions.backups ), honour dry_run , honour keep_both (save a diverged incoming session under a new id), and turn import off (with a warning in ProviderStatus ) on any format it doesn t recognise. Put pure parsing in a file without file-system access (like codex_format.rs ) so the web viewer can use it, and add it to messages_from_bundle . Add fixture files under crates/core/tests/fixtures/ tool / and tests: detect, list, read, export → import on a second fake machine (paths rewritten), update, local-ahead, conflict, running-process refusal, unknown format. Add the label in src/shared/types.ts ( PROVIDER_LABELS ). Badges, filters, push/pull, summaries and the viewer pick it up from there.
